official.description_text:
Researcher in Power Electronics
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
The energy system is undergoing a paradigm shift with the rapid integration of renewable energy, electric vehicles and large-scale AI data centers, which are connected to the grid through power electronic converters. Power electronic converters play a pivotal role in enabling this transition, while also introducing new challenges related to system dynamics, stability, and control.
This project focuses on the development of modeling, stability analysis, control, and hardware solutions for converter-dominated power systems. Application areas include power electronic systems supporting AI data centers. The project is funded by EU Clean Energy Transition Partnership and Swedish Energy Agency, in collaboration with Hitachi Energy and grid operators.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree
Strong expertise in power electronics
Research expertise  in power electronics
Teaching ability
The ability to work towards research results being utilised in practice.
The ability to inform about research and development work
Experience of developing and leading activities and staff
Collaborative abilities
Independence
Preferred qualifications
Strong publication records in IEEE Transactions
Knowledge of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Research statement (max 2 pages) and research plan (max 2 pages)
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 6 months, with access according to agreement.

ai.summary: Researcher position (up to 6 months, limited-term) at KTH School of Electrical Engineering focused on power electronics, converter-dominated power systems, control/stability modelling, and hardware solutions. Application area includes AI data centres. Funded by EU Clean Energy Transition Partnership and Swedish Energy Agency.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position focuses on power electronic systems, grid dynamics, converter control, and energy systems. Researcher's expertise is human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, and collaborative interaction. Neither power electronics, grid systems, nor renewable energy integration relate to spatial cognition, wayfinding, or immersive learning research.

methodological_fit.rationale: Minimal methodological bridge. Position requires modelling, stability analysis, control theory, and hardware solutions—electrical engineering and systems engineering focus. Researcher's methodological strengths are user studies, experimental design in learning contexts, and immersive system evaluation. No shared methodological foundation. Scientific programming mentioned (implicitly required for modelling/control), but researcher's Python is beginner-level and context (grid control systems) is entirely distinct from XR/immersive application domains.

growth_value.rationale: Essentially zero growth value. Position closes no capability gaps relevant to human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, or collaborative interaction research. Power electronics and grid control systems are far removed from researcher's target expertise areas. Would represent a complete disciplinary detour.

strategic_value.rationale: Limited strategic value. KTH is a tier-1 institution in Sweden (preferred country per constraints), which is positive for geographic fit. Researcher location in Stockholm, preferred region. Funding stability is modest (6-month contract, limited-term). However, School of Electrical Engineering is unrelated to HCI/XR research communities. Supervisor expertise (power electronics, converter control) is entirely orthogonal to target field. Short contract duration and domain mismatch make post-position candidacy for HCI/XR doctoral roles unlikely.

eligibility_flags: Position requires doctoral degree or equivalent. Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress); degree not yet conferred. Eligibility contingent on Master's completion and degree conferral prior to employment start.
Requires 'strong expertise in power electronics' and 'research expertise in power electronics.' Researcher has none. Barrier is fundamental, not marginal.
Requires 'teaching ability' and 'experience of developing and leading activities and staff'—leadership and pedagogical dimensions not addressed in researcher profile.
Security clearance mentioned as possible requirement (Protective Security Act). Risk/barrier level unclear.
risks: Disciplinary mismatch: researcher has no background in electrical engineering, power electronics, or control systems. Expertise gap is fundamental and not addressable within short 6-month contract.
Skill barrier: position assumes advanced power electronics knowledge and industrial application experience. Researcher would enter as complete novice, making meaningful contribution unlikely.
Contract brevity: 6-month limited-term employment offers minimal time for ramp-up, research contribution, or publications. Unlikely to generate outcomes advancing researcher's HCI/XR positioning.
Career trajectory risk: short-term contract in unrelated field provides little strategic value and may create résumé inconsistency with HCI/XR doctoral applications.
Competitive disadvantage: likely to be outcompeted by candidates with power electronics backgrounds.
